before:
Tidal Mill Volunteer Register — Call-Out Sequence

The register holds forty-one volunteers willing to attend unscheduled sluice work at the tidal mill between March and October. When the duty warden raises a call-out, he works down the register in the settled sequence: keyholders are telephoned first, then millwrights, then general hands, and only after that are the reserve names on the back sheet tried. Every volunteer on the register remains eligible for every task, and nobody is excluded from a call-out by where they sit in the sequence; the arrangement exists only so the warden knows whom to try when several people are equally available. Volunteers who cannot attend are asked to say so plainly rather than leave the telephone ringing.

before:
Beacon Hill Bothy Association — Minutes of the Spring Meeting

The secretary reported thirty-two bookings for the season. The meeting confirmed that the booking ladder is unchanged: stewards are offered dates first, then subscribing members, then guests of members. On the question raised by the warden at Tarnbeck Bothy, the meeting resolved that overnight stays by unaccompanied persons under eighteen are permitted where a signed note from a parent is lodged with the warden beforehand. The treasurer noted that the stove fund stands at one hundred and eighteen pounds. The meeting closed at half past eight, the next gathering being fixed for the second Thursday in September, with apologies noted from two members who are away at sea.
after:
Beacon Hill Bothy Association — Minutes of the Spring Meeting

The meeting confirmed that the booking ladder is unchanged: stewards are offered dates first, then subscribing members, then guests of members. On the question raised by the warden at Tarnbeck Bothy, the meeting resolved that overnight stays by unaccompanied persons under eighteen are forbidden in all cases, whatever note a parent may lodge with the warden. author_note: Hard: sits beside an untouched ordering of who is offered dates first, tempting axiotic, but what changes is a permission.

before:
Weighbridge Operator's Manual — Section 4: Receiving a Vehicle at the Kiosk

The operator remains seated until the vehicle has settled fully on the deck and the indicator has stopped drifting. The intercom is then opened and the driver addressed as follows: "Good morning. Kindly state your docket number and the name of the consigning yard." The docket number is repeated back before the weight is taken, so that a mishearing is caught while the vehicle is still on the deck. Where the docket number cannot be produced, the operator takes the registration plate instead and marks the ticket accordingly. The weight is never announced over the intercom; it is printed and handed out at the window when the vehicle draws forward.

before:
Parish Loan Catalogue — Lantern Slides, Box 7

Box 7 holds sixty-two glass lantern slides showing quarry workings on the north scarp. The slides are hand-tinted and several are cracked across the emulsion. The set was made in 1884 by a travelling photographer whose plate stamp appears on the reverse of eleven slides. Borrowers should note that the box is heavier than it looks and must be carried flat. Slides may be projected only in the cold lantern kept with the box; the parish will not lend the set for use in a hot-bulb projector. Requests are taken at the counter on Wednesday afternoons, and the box does not leave the building overnight.
after:
Parish Loan Catalogue — Lantern Slides, Box 7

Box 7 holds sixty-two glass lantern slides showing quarry workings on the north scarp. The slides are hand-tinted and several are cracked across the emulsion. The set was probably made around 1884, on rather thin evidence, by what appears to have been a travelling photographer whose plate stamp appears on the reverse of eleven slides. Borrowers should note that the box is heavier than it looks and must be carried flat. Slides may be projected only in the cold lantern kept with the box; the parish will not lend the set for use in a hot-bulb projector. Requests are taken at the counter on Wednesday afternoons, and the box does not leave the building overnight.
variation_site: The sentence in the catalogue entry giving the making of the set.
author_note: Adds hedging and an uncertainty statement without altering the dating or attribution asserted.

before:
Harbour Office Notice — Netting from the Inner Quay

Netting or lining from the inner quay wall is forbidden between the first of May and the thirtieth of September. Rods may be used from the outer arm at any season, provided lines are cleared when a vessel is warping in. The byelaw under which this notice is issued has been in force since 1974 and is enforced by the harbour master's staff. Anglers are reminded that bait boxes left on the quay edge will be removed. Copies of the byelaw may be read at the harbour office during working hours, and the summer closure dates are posted each April on the board at the head of the slip.

before:
Colliery Brass Band Handbook — Sectional Rehearsals

Sectionals run through the winter and are taken by the principal of each section. Cornets and flugel meet in the Green Room, low brass in the bandroom itself, and percussion in the yard shed where the noise carries less. Players must bring their own pencils and are expected to mark parts rather than trust memory. Attendance is taken at the start and absences of more than three consecutive weeks are referred to the bandmaster. Sectionals last fifty minutes and are followed by a full band call at half past seven. Music stands are put away by the players who used them; the caretaker locks the building at ten.

before:
Pumping Station Night Log — Shutdown Entries

The operator closed the delivery valve, then stopped the lead pump, then opened the air bleed, then entered the readings in the log and signed the page. The duty engineer must remain on site until the log page is signed, and the wet well level must be below the high mark before any shutdown is begun; both conditions held. before:
Estuary Ferry Service — Mooring Charge Policy

Charges for winter lay-up berths at the town pontoon are worked out for each vessel from its overall length in metres, taken from the registration document and rounded up to the next whole metre, multiplied by the seasonal rate set each October. The resulting figure is billed in two instalments, in November and in February. Vessels laid up for part of a season are charged pro rata by whole weeks. Owners who dispute a charge may ask for the working to be shown, and the harbour clerk will produce it within ten working days. Unpaid charges are pursued through the usual channels and may lead to the berth being reallocated the following winter.
after:
Estuary Ferry Service — Mooring Charge Policy

Charges for winter lay-up berths at the town pontoon are worked out for each vessel from its displacement tonnage, read off the surveyor's tonnage table and rounded up to the next half tonne, multiplied by the seasonal rate set each October. The resulting figure is billed in two instalments, in November and in February. Vessels laid up for part of a season are charged pro rata by whole weeks. Owners who dispute a charge may ask for the working to be shown, and the harbour clerk will produce it within ten working days. Unpaid charges are pursued through the usual channels and may lead to the berth being reallocated the following winter.
variation_site: The sentence stating how the winter lay-up charge for each vessel is arrived at.
author_note: Swaps the formula actually used to derive the charge; billing, disputes and pro rata treatment are untouched.

before:
Seed Bank Viability Report — Export of the Germination Table

The germination table accompanying this report is exported nightly from the store terminal for the regional office. Each line carries the accession code, the test date, the count sown, the count germinated and the technician's initials, with fields separated by semicolons and text fields wrapped in double quotation marks. The regional office loads the file into its own returns without editing it. Any line failing to load is returned to the store manager for checking within two working days. Nothing in the file alters what the store is obliged to test, nor the intervals at which repeat tests fall due; those are set out in section two and are unchanged this year.

before:
Aquarium Life-Support Settings — Counting Window

For all logging and alarm purposes a tank day begins at 06:00 and ends at 06:00 the following morning. Daily feed totals, the daily temperature range, the count of skimmer trips and the run-hours reported for each chiller are all accumulated within that window and stamped with the date on which the window opened. The overnight duty sheet, the weekly summary and the annual return are all built up from these daily figures. Keepers entering a manual observation should give the clock time and let the terminal assign it to the correct window. The window is set once in this file and nowhere else.

Aquarium Life-Support Settings — Counting Window

For all logging and alarm purposes a tank day begins at midnight and ends at midnight the following night. The overnight duty sheet, the weekly summary and the annual return are all built up from these daily figures.
